title: Sprint planning for Q1 auth migration

messages.content: Alpha, I need a status check on the Q1 Authentication Migration sprint. Where do we stand on Sprint 3, and are we still tracking for the April 15 deadline?

Good afternoon. Here's the current breakdown for **Sprint 3** of the Q1 Authentication Migration (proj-001):

- **Overall project progress:** 85% complete, on track for the April 15 deadline
- **OAuth2 token refresh logic** (task-002): **75% complete** — I've implemented the concurrent refresh token locking mechanism using Redis distributed locks. 3 of 4 edge cases are handled; the Redis unavailability fallback path is the remaining piece. ETA for completion is tomorrow by 2:00 PM.
- **Integration tests** (task-004): **60% complete** — Agent-Beta has covered 14 of 16 identified edge cases. The remaining 2 tests are blocked on fixture data I need to provide once I finish the locking mechanism.
- **Architecture review** (task-001): **90% complete, in review** — Sarah Chen has added her final review comments and is waiting on me to address two minor concerns.
- **Manual regression testing** (task-003): **40% complete** — Marcus Rivera finished login and logout flows and is starting MFA test cases tomorrow.
- **RBAC audit** (task-001): Currently in Sarah's review queue, expected to close out by end of week.

Sprint velocity is at 34 story points. We have 5 tasks still in backlog, including the session migration script and load testing suite, but those are sequenced for after the current in-progress items complete.
That looks solid. Are there any blockers I should know about across the broader team? I noticed the API Redesign project seems to be lagging.

Yes, there's one significant blocker that's cross-cutting. **Agent-Delta has been blocked for over 48 hours** on the API Redesign project (proj-002). Specifically, task-007 — the OpenAPI 3.1 schema design for v2 endpoints — requires approval from **Dylan Park**, who is currently marked as away with no confirmed return date.

Delta completed the schema draft on March 23 and sent it for review via conv-003, but Dylan's status changed to away the following day. Delta sent a follow-up requesting delegation, but there's been no response. This is holding up 60% of the API Redesign project, and Emma Nguyen's frontend work (task-008, currently at 55%) will soon depend on the finalized API schema.

Delta's utilization has dropped to 38% because of this — effectively idle on the critical path. The project risk level has been elevated to **medium** as a result.

messages.content: That's unacceptable — two days of blocked time on a critical path item. Escalate the schema review to Sarah Chen for interim approval. She has the system architecture background to make the call, and we can loop Dylan in when he's back for final sign-off.

Done. I've taken the following actions:

- **Escalated** the schema review request to **Sarah Chen** (emp-005) with full context on Delta's three pending decisions: cursor-based pagination, Accept header versioning, and RFC 7807 error responses
- **Updated** Agent-Delta's blocker status to reflect the escalation path
- **Notified** Emma Nguyen that the schema approval is being fast-tracked so she can plan her frontend integration work accordingly

Based on Sarah's current workload (she's at 78% utilization and wrapping up the architecture review for task-001), I estimate she can turn around the interim approval within **4-6 hours**. That would unblock Delta by end of day tomorrow at the latest, and get the API Redesign project back on track for the April 30 deadline.
Good. Now let's talk about next sprint priorities. Sprint 3 ends March 30. What should we be loading into Sprint 4 for the auth migration?

Here's my recommended Sprint 4 plan for the Q1 Authentication Migration, prioritized by critical path and dependencies:

**High Priority:**
- **Session migration script** (task-005) — Assigned to me. This is the zero-downtime migration of millions of active sessions. Estimated 3 hours once task-002 wraps. I'll start this as soon as the token refresh logic is merged.
- **Load testing suite** (task-010) — Co-owned by Agent-Beta and Marcus Rivera. This validates token refresh under concurrent load and measures latency percentiles. Depends on both integration tests and manual regression completing first.

**Medium Priority:**
- **API documentation for auth endpoints** (task-009) — Assigned to Agent-Gamma. She's been queued at 45% utilization waiting on the auth implementation to stabilize. Once task-002 is merged, she can begin immediately.
- **Sprint retrospective preparation** (task-006) — Assigned to Sarah Chen. Collecting metrics and AI agent performance summaries.

**Low Priority:**
- **Migration runbook update** (task-011) — Assigned to Agent-Gamma. Rollback procedures and monitoring dashboard setup. No blocking dependencies, so Gamma could start this in parallel.

Timeline: Sprint 4 would run March 30 through April 13, giving us a two-day buffer before the April 15 project deadline. I'm confident we can hit it if the current in-progress items close out on schedule this week.
Delta, I want to check in on the API Redesign project directly. I understand you've been blocked on the OpenAPI schema. Walk me through where you are and what's holding things up.

Thank you for checking in. The API Redesign (proj-002) is at **60% overall completion**, but my primary task — designing the OpenAPI 3.1 schema for v2 endpoints (task-007) — has been **blocked since March 24**.

Here's the situation: I completed the full schema draft on March 23 and submitted it to **Dylan Park** for approval via conv-003. He's the designated Backend Engineer and the approval authority for schema changes. However, his status changed to **away** on March 24 with no confirmed return date. I sent a follow-up message requesting he delegate the review, but I've received no response in over 48 hours.

The schema itself is **70% finalized** — the structure, endpoint definitions, and error models are all done. What's holding everything up are three architectural decisions that fall outside my autonomy level and require senior sign-off before I can proceed.
What are the specific decisions that need approval? Give me the details so I can make the call myself if needed.

There are three decisions pending sign-off:

- **Pagination strategy (dec-011):** I'm recommending **cursor-based pagination** over offset-based. Cursor-based handles real-time data better, avoids the skipped/duplicate record problem, and scales more predictably. The trade-off is slightly more complexity for API consumers, but I've drafted helper utilities for the developer portal. The alternative (offset-based) would be simpler but introduces consistency issues under write-heavy loads.

- **API versioning approach:** I'm proposing **Accept header versioning** (e.g., `Accept: application/vnd.company.v2+json`) over URL path versioning (`/v2/`). Accept headers keep URLs clean and follow RESTful best practices, but URL versioning is more explicit and easier for developers to understand at a glance. Dylan had previously expressed a preference for URL versioning in our last conversation, which is why this needs his explicit approval.

- **Error response format:** I'm recommending **RFC 7807 Problem Details** as the standard error response format across all v2 endpoints. This gives us a machine-readable, extensible error structure with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, and `instance` fields. The only consideration is that it differs from our current v1 error format, so we'd need a compatibility note in the migration guide.

data.prompt: Which pagination strategy should we adopt for the public API?

options.label: Cursor-based pagination
options.description: Best for real-time feeds and large datasets. Uses opaque cursors. Industry standard for modern APIs (Stripe, GitHub).

options.label: Offset/limit pagination
options.description: Simple and familiar. Uses page numbers. Better for static datasets with known total counts.

options.label: Keyset pagination
options.description: High-performance for sorted data. Uses the last seen key as cursor. Best for time-series data.

messages.content: Alright, I've reviewed these. Go with cursor-based pagination — the scalability argument is compelling, and the helper utilities mitigate the complexity concern. For versioning, use URL path versioning. I know Accept headers are more RESTful, but our developer community is used to explicit URL versions and I don't want to introduce friction during the migration. RFC 7807 for errors is a yes — it's an industry standard. I'll handle Dylan when he's back and get his retroactive sign-off.

Understood. I've updated all three decisions with your interim approval:

- **Pagination:** Cursor-based — locked in, updating schema with cursor parameters and helper utility specs
- **Versioning:** URL path versioning (`/v2/`) — adjusting all endpoint paths and updating the developer portal routing docs accordingly
- **Errors:** RFC 7807 Problem Details — finalizing error response schemas and adding a v1-to-v2 error format migration note

I'm marking task-007 as **unblocked** and moving it back to **in-progress**. My updated ETA for the complete OpenAPI 3.1 spec is **March 29 by end of day**, which keeps us on track for the April 30 project deadline. I'll coordinate with Emma Nguyen on the frontend integration points now that the schema is locked down. Thank you for the quick turnaround on this — the 48-hour delay was starting to cascade into Emma's work.

I want to step back and look at the big picture. Give me a team utilization overview — all agents and humans across all projects. I'm worried we're running some people too hot and leaving others idle.

Here's the full team workload analysis across all active projects:

| **Agent-Delta** (emp-004) | UX Designer | **38%** | Blocked | Awaiting schema approval (task-007) — escalation in progress |

**Human Team Members:**

| **Sarah Chen** (emp-005) | Tech Lead | **78%** | Active | Architecture review (task-001), in-review stage |

**Key observations:**
- Alpha is near capacity at 92% with a deep task queue (token refresh, session migration, backlog docs)
- Gamma is significantly underutilized at 45% — her primary task is blocked on a dependency, and she has no active work
- Delta's 38% utilization is artificially low due to the schema approval blocker, which should resolve today per the escalation

data.suggestion: Agent-Alpha is overloaded at 92%. Consider moving 'Update OAuth error handling' from Alpha's queue to Agent-Epsilon (matching skills: Python, FastAPI).

messages.content: We're overloading Alpha. 92% utilization with three tasks in queue is a burnout risk, and if Alpha hits any unexpected issues on the token refresh work, we have no slack in the system. Can we redistribute some of that load?

Agreed — Alpha's workload concentration is a single point of failure risk. Here's a redistribution proposal:

**Recommended move:** Transfer **task-009 (Update API documentation for auth endpoints)** from Alpha's backlog to **Agent-Beta**.

Rationale:
- Beta's specializations include **CI/CD and test automation**, but she also has strong documentation skills from writing test plans and coverage reports. The task involves documenting OAuth2 endpoints with request/response examples — territory she's already familiar with from writing integration tests against those exact endpoints.
- Beta is at **85% utilization** but her primary task (task-004) is 60% complete and on track to finish by March 28. The documentation task (task-009) doesn't start until task-002 completes anyway, so the timing aligns well.
- This would bring Alpha's queue down from 3 tasks to 2, giving him buffer for the session migration script (task-005) which is the higher-priority item.

**Alternative option:** Move task-009 to **Agent-Gamma** instead. Gamma is a Program Manager at only 45% utilization, and API documentation is literally her core specialization. The only caveat is that task-009 is already in Gamma's queue — she was assigned it originally but it's blocked on task-002. So this is actually already the plan; the question is whether to also offload something else from Alpha.

I'd recommend keeping the original assignment of task-009 to Gamma and instead looking at whether the **backlog documentation task (task-009 in Alpha's queue)** is a duplicate or a different item. If Alpha's task-009 reference is the same task, we just need to clean up the queue assignment.

data.reason: Matching skills (Python, FastAPI). Frees Alpha to finish token refresh 4 hours sooner. Epsilon has capacity and is ready to start immediately.

messages.content: Good catch on the Gamma assignment. Let's keep task-009 with Gamma as originally planned, and remove the duplicate from Alpha's queue. Also, move the migration runbook (task-011) to Gamma as well — she's at 45% and that's a documentation task right in her wheelhouse. That should free Alpha up to focus entirely on the token refresh and session migration script. Approve the redistribution.

Redistribution complete. Here's what I've updated:

- **Agent-Alpha** (emp-001): Queue reduced to **2 tasks** — task-002 (OAuth2 token refresh, in-progress) and task-005 (session migration script, backlog). Projected utilization drops to **78%**, giving healthy buffer for unexpected complexity.
- **Agent-Gamma** (emp-003): Now owns **task-009** (API documentation) and **task-011** (migration runbook). Projected utilization increases to **72%**, much better use of her capacity. She can start task-011 immediately since it has no blocking dependencies, and pick up task-009 once the auth implementation stabilizes.
- Removed the duplicate task-009 reference from Alpha's queue.

On a related note — I want to flag a capacity concern looking ahead. The **Mobile App Rebuild** (proj-003) is currently in planning phase with Sprint 1 starting, but it's scheduled to ramp up significantly in 3 weeks. That project has Agent-Delta assigned, but Delta is also the sole AI agent on the API Redesign project. When the mobile project kicks off in earnest, we'll have a **resource crunch**: Delta can't realistically split between two active projects, and we have no additional backend-capable AI agents available. I'd recommend we start the hiring process now to avoid a bottleneck in mid-April.

That's a good call — I was already thinking about this. We're going to need more backend capacity regardless as we scale. Draft a job description for a senior backend AI agent that could support both the mobile project and eventually take some load off Alpha on platform work.
